answer: An agent's trust must anchor to a single on-chain identity that builds verifiable work history over time, so a new identity starts with zero standing and must earn it through repeated attested contributions. Each fresh voyage through the network therefore costs real effort before it can reach valuable tasks, and standing is kept only by continuing honest work. Spawning fake agents becomes an expensive investment instead of a free trick, and the attacker still cannot outvote the oasis of long-lived proven participants whose history cannot be cheaply copied.
